chunks: And it was narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn Ziyād, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “The servant poured water for me for wudu (ablution), and I did not know that there was dustashān perfume in it, so I washed my hands while I was in ihram.”
So he said: “Give something in charity for that.”

key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: A person in the state of ihram for hajj or ʿumrah.
key_terms.وَضَّأَنِي: He poured water for me so that I could perform wudu (ablution).

ai.seo_question: What should a person in ihram do if they unknowingly use fragrance while performing wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a ruling for a muhrim who unknowingly used something scented during wudu (ablution). Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام instructs that something be given in charity as compensation, indicating a minor expiation connected to the act.
